[M157] [omnibox] Keep the focused look under the Full WebUI omnibox popup

Original change's description:
> [omnibox] Keep the focused look under the Full WebUI omnibox popup
>
> With the Full WebUI omnibox, the WebUI popup covers the location bar
> while it's open. Underneath it, LocationBarView still switched to its
> "popup open look" (no focus ring, an indented location icon, no location
> icon background, and hidden page actions). That look shows through as a
> "hollow" omnibox whenever the popup isn't painted on top of it:
>
> - On a new window, the popup widget is shown before the WebUI paints.
>   It's see-through until then, because the WebUI draws its own
>   background and shadow (kOmniboxFullWebUIShadow[1]).
> - On the window that loses activation, the popup hides a frame before
>   the location bar repaints.
>
> On Mac that's 1 to 4 frames per new window, which reads as a blink.
>
> Keep the regular focused look while the full popup (kFull) is open, so
> any frame where the popup isn't on top shows a normal focused omnibox.
> The AIM popup keeps today's behavior.
>
> Verified with frame-by-frame screen recordings of new windows on Mac and
> Linux: the hollow frames are gone.
>
> Test `LocationBarFocusRingHiddenInFullWebUIMode` expected the old look,
> so it's now `LocationBarFocusRingInFullWebUIMode`. It expects the ring
> under the full popup and no ring after blur, and it still checks that
> focus never moves to the native OmniboxViewViews.
>
> This leaves two smaller artifacts when the WebUI omnibox paints over the
> native location bar. Follow-up CLs will fix them:
>
> - The WebUI input row is bigger on every side than the
>   native focused location bar, so the ring grows outward when the WebUI
>   takes over.
> - In some new windows, the first frame or two of the WebUI
>   omnibox show a magnifier before the Google G, while the favicon
>   image loads.
>

[M157] [Omnibox] Add dogfood feedback button to the Full WebUI Omnibox

Original change's description:
> [Omnibox] Add dogfood feedback button to the Full WebUI Omnibox
>
> Adds a dogfood icon button to the Full WebUI Omnibox input, next to
> the debug dino. Hovering it shows "Submit Omnibox Dogfood Feedback",
> and clicking it opens Chrome's feedback form, which attaches a
> screenshot, the Chrome version, platform and system info. Reports
> use a new `kFeedbackSourceOmnibox` source and the `omnibox_webui`
> category tag. The tag is sent as the report's bucket and matches the
> "Omnibox WebUI Googler" bucket set up in gFeedback for Chrome desktop
> and ChromeOS, so reports land there.
>
> To make it clear that the feedback is about the omnibox, the form is
> opened with:
> - A pre-filled description: a go/omnibox-dogfood link, then the
>   standard bug template headings DESCRIPTION, REPRO STEPS, EXPECTED
>   RESULTS and ACTUAL RESULTS.
> - Extra diagnostics listing every feature with "omnibox" or "webui"
>   in its name, ignoring case, whose state was set by Finch,
>   chrome://flags or the command line, with its Finch group and params.
>   Features that keep their default state while tied to a trial (a
>   study's Default group) are labeled "default".
>   The list comes from base::FeatureList::GetFeatureOverrides(), so new
>   features are picked up automatically, and params are read without
>   activating trials. No user input is included.
> The UI is dogfood-only, so its text (the button's tooltip and the form
> template) is not translated.
>
> The button is gated on the new `Omnibox_DogfoodFeedback` param of
> `WebUIOmniboxFullPopup` (default false), so it can be enabled via
> Finch for dogfood populations. It can also be enabled locally with
> the "- with Dogfood Feedback" variation of
> chrome://flags/#webui-omnibox-full-popup.
>
> The WebUI calls a new `OpenDogfoodFeedback()` method on the popup
> PageHandler, because the popup WebUI can't open the feedback form
> itself.
> The form contents and diagnostics live in the new
> `omnibox_dogfood_feedback.{h,cc}`, with unit tests covering the
> feature filter and the diagnostics output.
>

[M157] omnibox: Skip permission prompt dismissal handling when popup is hidden

Original change's description:
> omnibox: Skip permission prompt dismissal handling when popup is hidden
>
> On macOS, hiding the browser window during teardown orders out child
> popup widgets before updating the parent window's visibility state.
> When an active permission prompt is attached to the AIM popup's
> WebContents, hiding the child widget marks its WebContents as hidden
> and triggers PermissionRequestManager::DeletePrompt() ->
> OnPromptRemoved(). Previously, HandlePermissionPromptDismissal()
> unconditionally refocused the location bar even when the popup was
> already hidden, triggering LocationBarView::ValidatePopupState(kAim)
> while the AIM widget was hidden and the parent browser widget still
> reported visible.
>
> Skip entering prompt dismissal mode and refocusing the location bar in
> HandlePermissionPromptDismissal() when IsShown() is false.
>

> [iOS] Reuse NotifyingView across window moves
>
> When Chrome enters the Tab Grid while in the background,
> -[TabGridTransitionHandler snapshotOfViewPortionAboveRect:middleRect:]
> snapshots _browserLayoutViewController.view with afterScreenUpdates:YES.
> UIKit's _performAfterContextCommitUnderCoverAllowDefer saves the layout
> constraints on ChromeOverlayWindow referencing the internal
> NotifyingView mirror before temporarily moving the browser layout view
> to a cover window, removing it from the cover window (window == nil),
> and restoring it to ChromeOverlayWindow before reactivating the saved
> constraints via _UIViewReactivatePotentiallyDisruptedConstraintsForView.
>
> Previously, addMirrorViewInWindow() and windowCoordinatesChangeHandler()
> called removeMirrorViewInWindow() and allocated a new NotifyingView
> whenever the observed view moved between windows, leaving the original
> NotifyingView detached (superview == nil) when UIKit reactivated the
> saved constraints on ChromeOverlayWindow.
>
> Reuse the existing mirrorViewInWindow instance in
> addMirrorViewInWindow() and only remove it from its superview when
> self.window becomes nil, preserving the instance until
> cr_onWindowCoordinatesChanged is cleared.

[M157] Use DynamicTo when downcasting clip path operation to reference clip

Original change's description:
> Use DynamicTo when downcasting clip path operation to reference clip
>
> In PaintClipPathAsMaskImage, the mask image painting loop iterates over
> a chain of clip path operations. On each iteration, it converts the clip
> path operation to ReferenceClipPathOperation using To<T>.

> the chain is not a ReferenceClipPathOperation (for example, a shape clip
> path such as circle() or inset()), To<ReferenceClipPathOperation> fails
> the type assertion and causes a crash.
>
> Using DynamicTo<ReferenceClipPathOperation> safely returns nullptr if
> the clip path operation is not a ReferenceClipPathOperation, allowing
> the loop to break gracefully.

Universal Opt-Out / GPC eligibility can change dynamically at runtime.
Previously, IsGPCExtensionEnabled() and ExtensionServiceImpl::Initialize()
assumed eligibility was static at startup. If a user was ineligible at
launch, ExtensionService was either not created or exited early without
setting up preference observers.

user is currently ineligible, ensuring preference change observers are
active. The extension itself is still only loaded when the feature is
actually enabled.

Original change's description:
> Fix SoftwareImageDecodeCache UAF
>
> SoftwareImageDecodeCache had a bug where if image decode tasks were
> stopped and restarted there could be a collision on
> ImageDecodeRequestId. If the CompositorFrameSink is lost the
> ImageDecodeCache object is recreated and
> ImageController::SetImageDecodeCache() runs. That calls
> StopWorkerTasks() which cancels pending decode requests but didn't
> cancel posted tasks. GenerateTasksForOrphanedRequests() then schedules
> new tasks reusing the same ImageDecodeRequestId range. If a posted
> ImageDecodeCompleted() from before StopWorkerTasks() runs and the
> ImageDecodeRequestId matches one of the new request there is a
> collision.
>
> The collision can result in a CacheEntry being deleted while there is
> still a pending request for it. Avoid collisions by cancelling all
> posted ImageDecocdeComplete() tasks in StopWorkTasks().
>

>

> manifest, the stored options stay behind. If an even later version
> declares the type again, the old stored value comes back instead of
> the new manifest default, although the extension never set it for
> that version.

> Stored options survive extension updates on purpose, so a user's
> choice made through the extension is not undone by an update. They
> only lose their meaning once the manifest stops declaring the type.

> not declare when an extension is installed or updated. The declared
> types are the ones setMimeHandlerOptions() accepts.
> The registry is now created with the profile, so it also sees
> installs that finish during startup.

[M157] [extensions] Add canEmbed to chrome.mimeHandler options

Original change's description:
> [extensions] Add canEmbed to chrome.mimeHandler options
>
> A MIME handler extension sets can_embed in its manifest to say whether
> it handles its MIME type inside iframes and embed or object elements.
> It cannot change this at runtime. An extension that wants to stop
> handling embedded content, or to start only after the user opts in, has
> to ship a new version with a new manifest. The only runtime option
> today, enabled, turns the handler off for top-level and embedded loads
> alike.
>
> Add an optional canEmbed member to MimeHandlerOptions. Both members
> default to the manifest entry's values until the extension sets them.
> The handler takes an embedded load only when enabled and canEmbed are
> both true, so enabled: false still turns it off everywhere.
> setMimeHandlerOptions() no longer requires enabled, and it changes only
> the members passed in the call.
>
> Agreed in the WebExtensions Community Group:
> https://github.com/w3c/webextensions/issues/1070#issuecomment-5697059532

> retaining a reference to `this` across Initialize().
> - Calling DisconnectSource() and stopping the renderer if Terminate()
> intervened during Initialize().

[M157] Lookalikes: don't defer non-HTTP(S) navigations for engaged sites

Original change's description:
> Lookalikes: don't defer non-HTTP(S) navigations for engaged sites
>
> LookalikeUrlNavigationThrottle::WillProcessResponse() defers the
> navigation until the engaged sites list has been loaded whenever the
> list is stale, which is always the case for the first navigations after
> browser startup. However, LookalikeUrlService::CheckUrlForLookalikes()
> ignores non-HTTP(S) URLs, so for navigations where neither the first nor
> the last URL of the redirect chain is HTTP(S) (the only URLs checked by
> PerformChecks()) the wait is pointless.
>
> This notably affects the New Tab Page at startup: in lab traces on a
> low-end Mac, the NTP navigation was deferred by ~40-170 ms waiting for
> the engaged sites list, delaying its commit and first paint.
>
> Proceed immediately for such navigations instead. The stored
> interstitial state is still cleared and interstitial reloads are still
> handled before this check, as before.
>
> The new behavior is guarded by the enabled-by-default
> kLookalikeSkipEngagedSitesWaitForNonHttp feature, which serves as a
> killswitch and allows measuring the impact with a Finch holdback.
